source.title: Optimiser Choice Can Amplify or Suppress Emergent Misalignment

record.file_problem: The complete LessWrong post is present, but it summarizes a linked paper whose full text is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports SFT-based emergent-misalignment results using narrow-task data and an EM measure, while varying optimisers and model size. It does not report every detail of the linked study's method.
record.gate_note: The post reports aggregate results for an optimiser sweep, a model-size comparison, and spectral regularisation. It gives few numerical rates and does not report the matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls from V1. It mentions RL only as future work. The four datasets in the main sweep are not identified in the post.
record.test_reason: The post reports EM rates from narrow SFT across 12 models (270M–235B) and a sweep of optimisers, datasets and batch sizes. These results bear on V7: how large EM is and how it depends on training choices and model scale. It gives no benign controls, in-context, RL, persona-direction, inoculation or benign-retraining results. Its mitigation, spectral regularisation of LoRA adapters, is not the V6 mitigation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors also conclude model size and family barely matter above 1B. They also argue a low-rank update may be necessary for EM, not just sufficient.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT on off-policy narrow-task data and an EM evaluation, but focuses on optimiser choice, model-size comparisons, and adapter-spectrum regularisation; the post does not give enough detail to confirm an exact match to the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimiser choice; adapter-spectrum regularisation; training loss; model size and family; learning rate and batch size are said to influence alignment through final loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Regularising the LoRA adapter towards a flatter spectrum recovers alignment for Adam and Lion, removes insecure-code EM under Adam, and worsens SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Penalising low-rank concentration of the adapter update mitigates EM for adaptive optimisers.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam and Lion concentrate the adapter update into few singular directions, while Muon spreads it. This ordering matches the alignment ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral concentration of the fine-tuning update predicts EM severity.

record.problems: The post is a secondary summary of the linked paper and gives no exact misalignment rates beyond the 7× spread. It omits the four dataset identities, most model-level and condition-level results, uncertainty estimates, and detailed evaluation methods. It does not report the matched benign controls needed for the full V1 claim.
record.rows_left_out: No separate model-by-model optimiser or dataset results are provided in the post. The post mentions that learning rate and batch size affect alignment through final loss but gives no separate values for those settings.

untested.parts: No secure-code or educational-insecure controls. No rate is given for the unregularised insecure-code Adam run.
Seed robustness, coherence filtering, and when EM appears during training.
The datasets are linked to Model Organisms for EM but are not named or reported separately.

missing.what: Sub-1B model EM rates, implied to differ from those of larger models.
missing.locator: What we found — Model size and family

missing.what: Per-dataset EM rates for the four Model Organisms EM datasets, plausibly medical, financial and other advice data, which would bear on V2.
Unregularised insecure-code EM rate under Adam.

record.verdict_notes: Linkpost summary; the full paper is not included. Spectral regularisation is a novel mitigation outside V6. The 270M–235B range covers 12 models, but the exact sizes are not listed.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report matched secure-code or class-requested insecure-code controls, nor exact rates against a base model.
The four datasets in the optimiser sweep are not identified as bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
The reported experiments use SFT on off-policy data; RL is suggested as future work.
The post reports adapter-spectrum measurements, not a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes.
The mitigation reported is spectral regularisation, not framing bad behaviour as requested during training or brief benign retraining.
The post does not report seed robustness, coherence-filter results, or when the effect first appears during training.
